title: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks

constraints.impact: Even O(n·k) brute force is only about 10⁴ steps, so it would pass. The sliding window is O(n) and is the pattern this problem teaches.
To make a window all black, you recolor each 'W' in it once. So the cost of a window is the number of 'W' in it, and one counter is enough.

constraints.meaning: The window length k is at least 1 and never longer than blocks.
constraints.impact: There is always at least one full window, so the answer always exists. It is at most k.

bruteForce.summary: for every start i, count the 'W' in blocks[i..i+k-1] from scratch and keep the smallest count. O(n·k) time.
